items.content_snippet: Today, AWS announces that AWS Security Hub now monitors Google Cloud Platform (GCP) resources, extending risk analytics, cloud security posture management, vulnerability management, and security response management across both clouds. Many AWS customers running workloads in AWS and GCP have had to operate separate security tools for each environment, making it difficult to prioritize risks holistically or respond consistently. items.title: AWS IAM announces Access Troubleshooter to debug access denied errors
items.content_snippet: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) introduces Access Troubleshooter , a new capability that gives you visibility into the full authorization context behind access denied errors so you can resolve them without trial-and-error. Previously, developers relied on the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the denying policy to debug a denial, with no visibility into the authorization context or other policies evaluated in the request that could contribute to the denial. items.title: Amazon ECR now replicates image deletions across regions and accounts
items.content_snippet: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports replicating image deletions and tag removals to your replication destinations. Previously, ECR replication copied images to destination regions and accounts but did not replicate deletions, requiring you to manage deletions separately in each location. items.title: Amazon EBS now supports associating additional KMS keys with snapshots
items.content_snippet: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) now supports associating additional AWS Key Management Service (KMS) keys with EBS snapshots. This new capability enables you to share and copy encrypted snapshots across accounts without first re-encrypting them, simplifying your disaster recovery and backup workflows. items.title: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports hybrid search combining vector and full text for more relevant search results
items.content_snippet: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports hybrid search that combines vector similarity search with full-text search within a single query. By combining semantic meaning and exact term matching into a single ranked list of results, hybrid search captures both intent and precise terms for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent memory, and search applications. items.title: Amazon Redshift now supports multi-statement transactions, conflict resolution, and time travel for Apache Iceberg
items.content_snippet: Amazon Redshift now supports multi-statement transactions, automatic write-conflict resolution, and time travel for Apache Iceberg tables. You can run multi-step, concurrent transformation pipelines directly on Iceberg tables and audit the results, with the transaction semantics you expect from a data warehouse. items.title: Amazon Connect Health medical coding is now available in public preview
items.content_snippet: Today, AWS announces the public preview of medical coding in Amazon Connect Health , a HIPAA-eligible AI service that works alongside healthcare teams across patient engagement and point-of-care workflows. Medical coding uses existing clinical documentation to suggest ICD-10-CM and CPT codes, including E&M levels and modifiers, for a provider or coder to review and approve before submission. items.title: Amazon Connect Customer agent assist now supports interactive responses
items.content_snippet: Amazon Connect Customer agent assist now supports interactive components, including cards, carousels, buttons, and input fields. The AI agent analyzes conversation context in real time, recommends actions, retrieves information, and executes tasks on behalf of contact center agents using MCP tools in Connect Customer or third-party services. items.title: AWS KMS now supports key sharing with AWS Resource Access Manager
items.content_snippet: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now integrates with AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM), giving you a simpler and more consistent way to share KMS keys across your AWS accounts, within your organization in AWS Organizations, and with specific IAM roles and users. You can now let trusted parties define the access they need through reusable managed permissions in RAM, while keeping full control of your keys and key policies. items.title: How Revolut’s lean teams take on bigger challenges with OpenAI
items.content_snippet: What can one engineer build when a project looks like it needs a whole team? At Revolut, an engineer used Codex to build an internal code review service himself. Its designers used Codex to turn seven years of design documentation into a format AI could read in a single day. OpenAI also helps Revolut’s financial crime team investigate flagged payments and respond faster to make shopping safer. Read the full story: https://openai.com/business/customer-stories/revolut/

items.title: How one engineer built a code review service with Codex | Revolut’s Dmitry Pitik
items.content_snippet: Dmitry Pitik thought he’d need a team of developers to build Revolut’s internal code review service. In this film, the Senior Platform Engineer explains how he broke the design into tasks, assigned them to Codex agents working in parallel and reviewed the code himself. That gave him more time for the engineering decisions he wanted to get right. Read the full story: https://openai.com/business/customer-stories/revolut/

items.title: Making marketing feel local across 40 markets | Revolut’s Kim Maniovich
items.content_snippet: A campaign that works in one market can need a different approach in the next. Kim Maniovich, Global Head of Business Marketing at Revolut, shares how her team uses AI to understand local differences and tailor campaigns faster. She also explains why she asks her team to challenge an answer even when it sounds convincing. Read the full story: https://openai.com/business/customer-stories/revolut/

items.title: Faster fraud response for safer shopping | Revolut’s David Abitbol
items.content_snippet: OpenAI helps Revolut’s financial crime team investigate flagged payments and respond faster to make shopping safer. David Abitbol, AI Lead at Revolut, explains how his team tests AI systems before putting them to work. He also shares how Codex gives engineers more time to weigh up different designs and decide what to build. Read the full story: https://openai.com/business/customer-stories/revolut/

items.title: Making seven years of design documentation AI-readable in a day | Revolut’s Dmytro Pavlov
items.content_snippet: Revolut’s designers had spent seven years documenting how their design system works. Senior Designer Dmytro Pavlov shares how his team used Codex to turn that material into a format AI could read in a single day. Along the way, they spotted gaps in their templates and made the guidance clearer for the designers who use it. Read the full story: https://openai.com/business/customer-stories/revolut/

items.title: How Check Point speeds up vulnerability research with Daybreak | OpenAI for Cybersecurity
items.content_snippet: Check Point CTO Jonathan Zanger explains how his team uses OpenAI Daybreak to analyze vulnerabilities and turn findings into protections for customers. A vulnerability research workflow that once took hours can now be completed in minutes, according to Zanger. Watch the full video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVVdxMwPBuA Read the full customer story: https://openai.com/index/check-point-daybreak/
